utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we left off before the break that you testified that you had become a member of the 2nd Mostar Battalion of the ABiH army. My next question will be what -- do you know what happened on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 9 May 1993, around -- around 6.00, 6.30 - I don't know exactly myself any more - the HVO launched an attack against the ABiH positions, that is, against the headquarters of the 4th Corps of the ABiH in -- at the Vranica building, and I was there. First there was an artillery attack which was followed by an infantry attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were at the Vranica building on the morning of the 9th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in the building itself. I was in the complex. This was in the logistics centre, which was part of that complex. So I climbed up on the roof and across the rooftops I crossed over into the headquarters building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did you actually climb up on the roof of the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was sometime in the afternoon, around 1.00 or 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay on the roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For at least five or six hours. Let's say I was there from 2.00 until about 8.00, when this got dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you stay for such a long time on that roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there was a lot of -- there was a lot of shelling. There was a lot a fire directed at the building from the anti-aircraft machine-guns, and throughout this time there was daylight. So it was not worth trying to get off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when it got later and it got darker, you were able to get into the building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Again we used an area where the elevator room was, and from there through an opening which was made by the anti-aircraft gun, we were able to climb back down into the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown Exhibit 16.4, please. We're not getting a very clear picture on the monitor. I'm not sure whether that's only this monitor or -- there seems to be a reflection. Yes, that's better. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see the residential complex and two kiosks. I see also two vehicles. And this was -- this building was call the Vranica building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please, with the pointer, indicate where on the roof -- where you spent this afternoon on the 9th of May on the roof, on which spot on the roof.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here, on this part of the roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And from here you can see the protruding house -- the housing for the elevator, and this is where the brigade was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the location of the headquarters in this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was right here underneath; that is, the brigade command was right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be on the second floor? You are pointing at the second or the third floor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot see where it was from the greenery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on which floor of the building was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was actually not on any of the upper floors. It was in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the headquarters was situated in the basement, and the rest of the floors were all occupied by residents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what happened the next day, on the 10th of May? Did the attack continue on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attack continued on the morning of the 10th of May. It was still more intense. They started firing at the apartments where people were living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time that fire broke out in the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this was only after the third or fourth attack when the bullets had been fired in the basement where the inhabitants were. It was then that we withdrew to the upper floors. It was then that they started shooting at the apartments, and bullets pierced through the windows and doors to the areas where the civilian population was. And from these bullets, one RPG had incendiary bullets, and it was -- that building caught fire. And I think this was sometime around 2.00 or 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when the situation became hopeless and that you decided to surrender?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. A leading and suggestive question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have all heard things like this. Maybe you could rephrase your question a little bit, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that about 2.00, 3.00 fire broke out. Where were you at that time and with whom were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, we were all together. I cannot recall on which floor we were, but we all hid behind the elevator. There was an area behind there, and that is where bullets couldn't reach us easily. We somehow tried to put out the fire, but because the shells had burst the hydrants, we couldn't, and the situation was not such that we could successfully put out the fire. And at one point, we decided to surrender -- that is, not to surrender, but to get out of the building with the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, so you said that you were going to get out with the civilians, out of the building. Did you at that time wear a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I changed my clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you change it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they broadcast through loudspeakers that they would kill us all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you went out of the Vranica building? First of all, how big was the group of people who went out of the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All people -- all the people who found themselves in those apartments, about 20, 30 soldiers -- there's a yard behind the building. And we had to come out with our hands on our heads and to walk towards the School of Economy -- Economics, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the photograph. You said you were taken out, and you had to move to the School of Economics. Where would the School of Economics be situated in relation to the Vranica building as it has been depicted here? Would it be on the front side of the building or on the back side of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was here, in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a bit difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. Thank you. Now, when you were gathered at the School of Economics, who was there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness also be advised to move a bit closer to the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you would have to move a little bit closer to the microphone so the interpreters can hear you better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were civilians, children, elderly, all kinds of people. I don't know how many, but there were also children among them and elderly, young people, old people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were the soldiers that had captured you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally was captured by Juka, with some other members of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there also other brigades, except for Juka and the Convicts Battalion, who were there at the school of economics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not at the school of economics. On the 9th of May, the first attack, that was a brigade from Capljina, and there was also some special police who took part in the attack. And also from the 3rd Simska Battalion. I can't recall all their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the school of economics, it was Juka and a unit which you called the Bosanska Bojna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Juka was a part of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- was this the first time you met Juka or did you know this person you called Juka from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the first time that I was that close to him, but I knew who he was even before, even though we did not know each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come that you knew him even if you had not met him before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1992, he was a hero of the city of Mostar. All media wrote about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you mean to say that you saw photographs of him in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw photographs in newspapers, but I also saw him walking around in Mostar prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did Juka do at the school of economics? What happened to you and the rest of the people who were guarded there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First they told all the Croat men and women that they were free to go wherever they wanted. I don't know whether he -- the Serbs were told the same. And the elderly Muslims and women were told that they would be escorted to the Velez stadium, and the rest of us who were fit for military service were left there in front of the school of economics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people of military -- Muslim men of military age were left? How big was this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were about 30, 35. I don't know exactly myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we were taken to the Tobacco Institute where the main HVO headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far a walk is that from the school of economics to this HVO headquarters at the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If it please the Court, I don't think the interpreter got that question correctly, but I object to the question and in the form of the question. It assumes facts not in evidence, and now I'm looking at the translation. I don't think the translator got the exact question. So ... Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I don't understand this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't understand it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the objection because it's showing up different than the way I heard it. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I need to repeat the question or do you remember the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me the distance between -- the distance between the school of economics and the Tobacco Institute. I would say it's about 20 minutes, 20 minutes on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the Tobacco Institute, who was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived at the Tobacco Institute, the whole leadership of the so-called HZ HB, that is, the whole military leadership of the HVO was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of these people, and if so, could you give me their names and their function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Brano Kresic [as interpreted]. He was the chief of SIS or the police. Then Bozo Rajic was there. At that time he was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. If you're going to mention names, the court reporters will have to record it, and so I'm going to ask you if you spell out -- if you mention a name, if you could say it either very carefully or spell out the name so that the court reporters can report it in an accurate way. Sorry to interrupt. I think you were referring to -- the first person you referred to was a man named Branko Kvesic. Could you spell that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B-R-A-N-K-O, first name, K-V-E-S-I-C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in charge of all the police of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue. Any other names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next name was Bozo Rajic, again, B-O-Z-O, R-A-J-I-C. I think at that time he was the spokesperson for the government or something. I know that he was some kind of a spokesman there. I saw Petar Zelenika, P-E-T-A-R, Z-E-L-E-N-I-K-A. He was a high official with the HVO. I don't know his exact position. And I don't know the names of others, but some were wearing civilian and some military outfits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the first person you mentioned was Branko Kvesic. Was he the same person who was your chief when you were working for the SIS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived there at the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived at the Tobacco Institute, Branko Kvesic, when he saw me, approached me and said, How could you leave without asking me? You could have told me about it, and we could have found some solution. I told him that I did not want to shoot at my own people. Right after that, I cannot recall exactly now, but I think to his left or to his right, because there was a whole group there, he suddenly called over Tuta and said, "Look at this. He was with us, and then he turned his weapon and started shooting at us."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a person named Tuta. Had you seen this person before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know from the newspapers, but I know that at that time he only referred to him as "Tuta".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know his full name as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that his surname is something like Naletilic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know what his function was at the time that you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he had formed that brigade, the Convicts' Battalion, at Siroki Brijeg, and he was the top man there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you had seen him before. Where had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he used to come to Branko Kvesic at the SIS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you describe the man, Tuta, at the time that you saw him at the Tobacco Institute. Do you know what he was wearing and how he looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had many-coloured trousers. I don't know what kind of clothes he had above the waist. He had spectacles, and his hair was pepper and salt. He looked older than he really was. Long hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said a moment ago that Mr. Kvesic spoke to Tuta, and that he said something to Tuta. Could you repeat what Mr. Kvesic said to Tuta and what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Branko Kvesic said to Tuta that I had been with them, and that after that, I had turned my rifle on them. And then Tuta approached -- he had a Motorola in his left hand and began to hit me on my forehead and swear at my balija mother. And so three or four blows after that, when I said that my mother was a Catholic, he got even angrier and struck me several more times after that with the Motorola. And it had an aerial. He drew a cross on my forehead and said he would sentence me to death to serve as an example to others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were hit by his Motorola. Where were you hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the left side on my forehead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times were you hit on that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some three or four times by the time that I said that my mother was Catholic. And after that, another three or four times, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you suffer any injuries from this hitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was perspiring so that my skin was slightly damaged, but I didn't bleed or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did Tuta do after this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean, when he sentenced me to death, or after that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, when he -- yes, after that. What did he do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. Well, we lined up, and as was his custom, then he approached Pobric. I don't know what he told him. But at that moment, he suddenly hit him with the Motorola on his head, and he started bleeding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sorry to interrupt you. You said that he approached another person. Could you repeat the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pobric, P-O-B-R-I-C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell me, what did you see of this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was in the same line, all I could see was how he talked, how he started to hit him, how blood oozed. And then Juka said, Don't. Let him be. He'll come with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that this man named Pobric was bleeding after this beating. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while this beating went on, were any of -- were there other HVO soldiers present as well? And the persons you have been referring to, the people you just referred to earlier, were they all present during this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were present, those -- Juka's soldiers. And with them were Slezak, if that's his name, and Dujimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to go into private session for some minutes, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what's the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the witness to identify some of the persons who were also in this group of 30 to 35, who were in there, and I think these names would be better mentioned in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, after you saw Tuta beat Mr. Pobric, did a man arrive by the name of Mladen Misic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this man do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As he entered the factory -- whilst he was still in the yard, he shouted, "Give me ten to shoot them. Oh, no, what ten? Give me all of them to shoot them dead." Juka then said to him that he should capture his own prisoners and do with them as he pleased, but that these prisoners here were to be exchanged for his men in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened to you after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that Dujmovic, Slezak, and two or three other soldiers who were with Juka came to me and started to beat me with their hands and rifle butts, and if I fell to the ground, they hit me with their rifle butts until I stood up, and then they repeated three or four times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you were beaten by Juka, was Tuta still present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did Juka at one moment interfere while you were being beaten by his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He helped me to stand up, put me in the line, and said, "Nobody will harm you again." And then he suddenly swung on his feet and kicked me in the head. And after that, I was left alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the Tobacco Institute, was there also a camera crew present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To my left -- no, to my right there was a HTV crew with a camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to show the witness Exhibit number 17, which is a video clip from the Croatian television, and I think I would like to show this in private session since it will identify the witness, and I think -- I don't know whether we should do it in closed session or private session, but I -- it should definitely be at least in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, Plaintiff's Exhibit 17 has just been identified by my learned colleague as a video clip from a TV station and that has never been delivered to the Defence. It has?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think all those documents, photos, and the videotapes have been furnished to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll check, but my colleagues inform me that this has not been given to us. Just to indicate for the record, Your Honour, that we have looked at all the videotapes that we have received from the Prosecutor, but we have not come across this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott. Do you have anything to say on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, our records will show that at the very beginning of the trial when the binders were provided, all the videotapes went over. There was a large -- there was a box of videotapes, and I'm confident -- I could be wrong without having an opportunity to clarify this, but as I stand here, I'm confident that all those videotapes were turned over. Now, we'll make inquiries into our records to verify that. That's all I can say it at this point. I would fully expect that it was turned over some time ago. In fact, it was probably even before the trial -- it was before the trial started because it was back during the deposition proceedings, because all those binders -- as the Registry will remember, binder one was used during the depositions and all those videotapes were turned over back then. So this was at the end of the July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I confirm that we received the last batch of videotapes during the deposition, because the Defence requested those clips as we were interested in them, and we went through all of them, and in that box with the videotapes, I did not find a single one. Perhaps there are several different recordings, but if I understood my learned friend, an HTV recording, no, we did not get that tape. Perhaps it's a mistake. I'm not accusing anyone, but we did not see it amongst the evidence that we have, because we absolutely went through all the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, so far as I remember that this Trial Chamber made a decision at the meeting that those maps, photos, and videotapes from P1 to P53,are admitted and there were no objections from the Defence. counsel If you are not sure about this particular tape, I hope you could allow us to have it shown in this courtroom, and you have your right to make any objections that may come across this issue in the tendering of this videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, we are talking about two types of evidence that we are getting from our learned friends, and we never managed to go through them, because on Sunday we were given two binders and they announced eight more. We simply have no time to go through all of them. And this applies to 17 binders that were received on Friday. And the videotapes were given to us during the depositions. And I repeat, the Defence did go through all these videotapes and there were no HTV tapes about Vranica. That is all we are saying. I think we simply should have been shown it so that we could know what it is about. I'm not saying that -- my learned friends perhaps think that they gave them to us, because it's a huge amount of evidence. That is something that I said right at the beginning of the case in those 17 binders. Your Honours, we've just finished going through those documents and translating them. We had to do it by ourselves in spite of all this effort that we have to put in here, and I'm constantly fearful that I might -- that I might damage my client. I may have perhaps done damage to my client, because when I didn't object to the maps, I said I wouldn't object to maps and photographs and the videotapes that I managed to see, but this does not go for those that I never saw. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may for a moment, what I wanted to say is that I don't think we should be having this broader discussion now with the witness. We have a witness here. If Mr. Krsnik wants to debate documents, we can do that whenever the Trial Chamber chooses to schedule that. And the only other point that I'm going to make is that in binder number one, as for Exhibit number 17, surrogate sheet - I've just taken it out of our binder. It's the same in every binder - it says "Video of Mostar, Video clip of 9 May 1993, Vranica attack and captured ABiH soldiers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 17 says "Reserved number," if I remember correctly or my learned friend will correct me if I am wrong. It says "Reserved number," but there is no tape. That is so, Your Honours. It says "Reserved number," but we did not get the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after consultations amongst the Judges, we have decided that to the fairness of Defence counsel, we believe that they are entitled to watch it. We don't care what is the reason for that, why you have not received it or have not seen it, but I will give you a chance to watch it for five minutes. So this Chamber will adjourn until five minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. --- Break taken at 3.24 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness AA, where were you taken next after the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the Tobacco Institute, they brought a bus. They boarded us and took us to Listica, in front of the civilian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown Exhibit 26.4, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, Witness AA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the civilian MUP building in front of which they brought us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where were you put? You said you were put in front of the building. Where was this? Can you indicate that with a ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately here where this vehicle is and a bit to the right. Let's say in front of this second set of barred windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this the whole group who was also taken to the Tobacco Institute were taken to the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened when you were lined up in front of the MUP station? Witness AA, you don't have to be that close to the microphone. If you keep about half a metre distance, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were met there by the regular police. There were two or three of Juka's men, and in front of the MUP building there was -- I believe at that time he was something, either Tuta's deputy or he was leading one of Tuta's units. I cannot remember his name, but I can describe him. He was shortish, dark, and he was wearing a Spitfire jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did this man do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person whose name I told you I didn't know, and he had some rank, and he either led a unit or was a deputy. He was close to Tuta. He approached Meho Zilic - Meho, first name, Zilic, last name, Z-I-L-I-C - and he told he was a member of Kosen [phoen]. He was always killing Croats, and he cursed him, that he had always hated Croats, and then he hit him with the handle of his pistol and knocked out his two teeth. Then he asked whether anybody had taken part in the liberation of the left bank of Mostar. I raised my hand. He asked me whether I was on Mount Hum. I told him that the Mount Hum had nothing to do with the liberation of the city of Mostar, and then he hit me several times. Then they took us to the police building. All our personal effects were taken away from us, and they took us down to the solitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be now shown Exhibit 26.7 and 26.8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you were taken down to the basement of the MUP station. Were you then put in a cell, and could you please see if you recognise the photograph which has been put on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was the cell to which they took us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with how many people were you put in this cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that there was another cell next to this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And show the other exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This the other cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see some squares in the wall. What were those squares?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were blocks that were placed there. They served for airing, for ventilation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If we can put the other photograph on there again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This one only has one block, and this was the cell you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in this cell, but I have to say that this up there did not exist, these blocks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened during that evening when you were taken into the cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a certain period of time, Romeo Blazevic, B-L-A-Z-E-V-I-C, and Ernest Takac, T-A-K-A-C, came into the cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know these persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had not known Ernest Takac, and I did know Romeo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who do you believe -- what did you know from Romeo Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that he did not have an impeccable record. He was a small-time hood, thief, and he had a cafe. I know that both of them were Stela's men. They were in Stela's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that they were both in Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody in Mostar knew about it. It wasn't any special knowledge. I don't know how to explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened when Romeo Blazevic and Ernest Takac entered the cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Romeo Blazevic held a koblac in one hand, and Ernest Takac walked in with a hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in his hand he had a koblac. What kind of instrument is that? Can you describe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a stick. And at its top, it has a metal ball. And that ball is filled with lead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened when -- what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Romeo approached me. First he hit a man who was next to the wall. He approached me and accused me of having blown up his cafe and wanted to hit me with this koblac. I tried to protect myself several times. He pulled out a pistol, and he said that if I was to raise my hand again, that he would shoot me. I did not obey him, and I kept backing up. Then I tripped over the platform. Then he approached -- I fell, and then he approached me and hit me over the head with his pistol handle. And he broke my skin, and my head was full of blood. And then he did not touch me after that any more. But I received no medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he only hit you with the pistol or did he also hit you with the koblac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He hit me with the koblac as I was protecting myself; but after I had fallen, then he hit me with the pistol handle on my right side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Ernest Takac was there as well? What did Ernest Takac do at the time that you were beaten by Romeo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He stood at the door, and he said, Come on, let's go. I will just toss in the hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you were detained in the MUP station, were you -- after a few days, were you taken out to do forced labour and where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three or four days later, five of six or us were called out of the cells. We were told that -- to board a truck and that we were going to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then on the way, they said that they were kidding, and that we were being taken to work on Tuta's pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit 26.10, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you recognise what's depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's the pool where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you referred to it as Tuta's pool. Why do you refer to it as Tuta's pool?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that. They told us that we were going to work on Tuta's pool. The home guards who led me there said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have to do when you were taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I guess the pool had not been used for years, and there were rocks and there was a lot of weed around it. There was earth at the bottom of it, so we had to clean it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days did you work at this pool?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not work more than three or four days on this pool.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the second day that you were working there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second or the third day -- I am not sure one which of those two -- here, on the far end, this is where we were placing rubbish. And then Tuta came to the pool across this bridge. Everybody laughed. And I know he had condemned me to death, so I was scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have a clear view of Tuta? Because you said you were there in the corner, and I can see all these trees over there. But you were able to see Tuta? You were able to identify him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You did not -- you did not need to see Tuta. As he stepped off and on to the bridge, everybody started clapping and cheering him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when you found out that Tuta was at the pool?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he arrived at the pool, I had a wheelbarrow. I hid with it behind, and I covered myself with it. And they started shooting, but they were shooting -- they were not aiming at anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tuta talk with any of the prisoners who were working there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall another incident which happened at the pool the day after or on any other day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I sat here at the pool, and Taso was to the left of me. And a man saw me. And when he saw me, he started hurriedly in my direction. And I said, I'm in trouble now. And at that point, this man approached me and kicked me in the chest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who this man was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know his name, but I used to see him. He was the driver for the Minister of Social Affairs at the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this man do to you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As soon as he crossed that bridge, he approached me and just kicked me without saying anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were sitting on the edge of the pool. Were you with your back to the pool or with your face towards the pool?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had my back to the pool.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after he kicked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After he kicked me, I fell. As I had my back to the pool, I hit my head against the concrete. He jumped into the pool after me to continue beating me. I defended myself. I ran, and I ran to this corner here so I could protect myself better there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I defended myself, he pulled out a pistol and wanted to kill me. At that moment, a man called Jablanica appeared. He jumped into the pool and grabbed him by the hand in which he was holding the pistol and chased him away. Did he not allow him to touch me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this incident, did you -- as a result of this incident, did you no longer have to work at the pool?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that incident, I in longer worked at the pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, I can leave it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.03 p.m.,
